title: Tryouts and Locker
premise: Jude Quintana has kept her anonymous coding account — and her identity as the daughter of a disgraced whistleblower — hidden for twelve years, until a teacher pairs her with Priya Nair, her academic nemesis, for a semester project that forces them to build an app together. When Priya discovers Jude's anonymous account and threatens to expose it, Jude realizes Priya isn't her enemy at all but someone carrying her own inherited secrets. As the deadline looms and their fragile alliance deepens into found family with a ragtag coding club, Jude must decide whether to unmask herself publicly, reclaiming her father's legacy on her own terms — or stay safe and lose everyone she's come to love.
about_author: Lena Villalobos is a former software engineer who traded debugging production code for debugging teenage hearts. She writes from a cluttered desk in Tucson, where she mentors first-generation coders and collects vending machine toys.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Careful
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. She navigates another invisible day at Westfield High, monitoring her anonymous account @quintanatruth from the library's back terminal. A near-miss with a classmate who almost sees her screen establishes her hypervigilance. Emotional beat: the exhausting weight of a secret that has become her whole personality.

chapters.title: The Pairing Nobody Wanted
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Ms. Okafor announces the semester capstone: build a working app in pairs, and she reads the list aloud — Jude and Priya Nair. Priya's sneer in the hallway afterward is pure venom. Jude's stomach drops. Emotional beat: dread, the sense that her careful architecture is about to be breached.

chapters.title: Nemesis Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. We learn why Priya hates Jude: three years of being edged out at hackathons by someone she suspects isn't even trying. Priya's own pressure — a mother who runs a failing startup and calls Priya her 'second chance' — reframes her cruelty as fear. Emotional beat: the enemy is a mirror.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The first project meeting in the empty computer lab is a negotiation of hostilities: they divide the app into non-communicating halves. Jude proposes a study-buddy scheduler; Priya demands something 'actually impressive.' They compromise on a mental health check-in tool neither will admit they need. Emotional beat: armed truce.

chapters.title: Locker 214
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude finds an unsigned note in her locker: 'I know who you are.' Panic spirals — is it about her father, her account, or a prank? She changes all her passwords at 2 a.m. and lies to her mother at breakfast for the first time in years. Emotional beat: the secret's first crack showing.

chapters.title: The Third Chair
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya drags in Dev, a sweet, chaotic junior who can't code but can draw, and Marisol, a quiet sophomore who tests better than both of them. The pair becomes a four-person club by accident. Jude resents the expansion; Priya pretends it's strategy. Emotional beat: found family forming against both their wills.

chapters.title: What the Account Knows
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya, troubleshooting Jude's half of the app, finds a cached session logged into @quintanatruth. She doesn't confront Jude — instead she reads twelve years of posts and learns about the whistleblower father, the lawsuits, the shame. Emotional beat: knowledge as a loaded weapon Priya isn't sure she wants to fire.

chapters.title: Midterm of Small Betrayals
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Midterm grades post; Priya beats her by two points for the first time ever, and Jude realizes she's been sandbagging to stay invisible — and that Priya knows. A screaming match in the parking lot ends with Priya saying, too quietly, 'I know what you post at midnight.' Emotional beat: the threat made explicit.

chapters.title: The Note Writer
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev confesses to the reader (not the group) that he wrote the locker note — he'd recognized Jude's coding style from a cached forum post and thought it was a cool icebreaker. He watches Jude flinch at every note since and can't figure out how to undo it. Emotional beat: comic relief curdling into guilt.

chapters.title: All-Nighter Protocol
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A demo deadline forces the four into Marisol's garage for an all-nighter. Pizza, terrible playlists, and 3 a.m. honesty: Priya admits her mother's startup is dying and the capstone is Priya's scholarship lifeline. Jude almost tells her secret back. Almost. Emotional beat: intimacy at the edge of confession.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude visits her father, who now manages a hardware store and never talks about the scandal that gutted their family. She asks him, for the first time, whether he regrets it. He says: 'I regret that you learned to hide before you learned to speak.' Emotional beat: grief reframed as inheritance — she can choose what to carry.

chapters.title: The Leak
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya's mother finds @quintanatruth open on Priya's laptop and recognizes the name Quintana instantly. She pressures Priya: expose the account, go viral, save the startup with attention. Priya refuses — and her mother threatens to do it herself. Emotional beat: Priya inherits her own impossible choice.

chapters.title: Labels Off
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The school's anonymous gossip account starts dropping hints about 'a certain junior's family.' Jude assumes Priya leaked. She tears the group apart in the lab, saying things she can't take back, and quits the project. Emotional beat: self-sabotage at the moment of closest approach; the found family shatters.

chapters.title: What Marisol Saw
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol reveals she saw Priya's mother photographing Jude's laptop at the garage night — and that Marisol said nothing because she was scared of losing her first friends. She brings the group evidence. Emotional beat: the quiet one finds her voice, and the truth reroutes the blame.

chapters.title: Deadline Week
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya publicly defies her mother at the startup's investor demo, refusing to trade Jude's secret for funding. The startup's collapse becomes real; Priya comes to Jude's door soaked in rain, holding the app on a flash drive. Emotional beat: sacrifice as apology; the nemesis becomes the ally.

chapters.title: The App That Tells the Truth
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Reconciliation in the lab: they finish the app together — a check-in tool that lets users share struggles anonymously or by name, their choice. The design debate becomes the thematic argument: is anonymity safety or a cage? Jude codes the 'reveal your name' feature with shaking hands. Emotional beat: the app becomes her decision made visible.

chapters.title: Viral
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Priya's mother leaks @quintanatruth anyway, and the school — then the internet — erupts. Jude's father's old scandal resurfaces; reporters email the school. Jude stays home, watching her twelve years of careful burn down in an afternoon. Emotional beat: the worst-case scenario arriving, and being survivable.

chapters.title: Assembly
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The principal calls an assembly about 'online conduct,' implicitly shaming Jude. Instead of hiding, Jude walks to the front, takes the mic, and tells the school who she is: the coder, the daughter, the person behind the account — on her own terms, in her own words. Emotional beat: the climax; hiding ends by choice, not exposure.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Annotated
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The fallout: some cruelty, unexpected support, a local journalist who frames Jude's father as brave. Priya's mother, humiliated by the failed leak, begins her own hard reckoning. Priya and Jude sit in the locker bay — locker 214 — and laugh for the first time. Emotional beat: the labels come off and the people underneath fit together.

chapters.title: Demo Day
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The capstone presentation: the four present the app, and Jude demonstrates the name-reveal feature by logging in as herself, live. The room goes silent, then Ms. Okafor gives them the only standing ovation of the day. Emotional beat: the private arc made public and celebrated; craft as courage.

chapters.title: What We Keep
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Epilogue-flavored: summer begins. Dev sketches the four of them at the garage; Marisol starts a coding camp for middle schoolers; Priya's mother takes a job she doesn't hate. Jude's account posts one final time — not anonymously. Emotional beat: found family as the inheritance she chooses.

chapters.title: Tryouts
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, final chapter. A new semester: Ms. Okafor asks Jude to mentor the next capstone class. A terrified freshman with a secret of her own reminds Jude of herself. Jude slides a note into the girl's locker — a kind one this time. Emotional beat: full circle; the careful years become the foundation for someone else's courage.
